title: Console slimline MVP: reduce dashboards, tracing & cost-breakdown surface and acceptance criteria
creator: Maya Chen
summary: Scope down the Console observability surface to a slimline MVP that prioritizes actionable cards for latency, errors, and cost while deferring heavy tracing and deep cost analytics to later phases.
background: Multiple PM/Design/Eng discussions in Feb exposed that the original Console telemetry scope is too broad to deliver in the next release window without risking stability and cost. We need a defended minimal surface that delivers end-user value for debugging regressions and monitoring cost leakage while keeping engineering lift low. The goal is a pragmatic MVP that can be shipped behind a feature flag and iterated based on usage and qualitative feedback.
problem_statement: Current Console PRD contains >12 dashboard tiles, full span trace collection, and per-token cost breakdowns for all routes. Delivering all of that would delay launch and increase backend ingestion and storage costs. We must define precise cuts and acceptance criteria so engineering can implement a safe MVP.
proposal: Deliver a compact Console telemetry MVP with: (1) three actionable dashboard cards (Route Latency P95, Route Error Rate, Top-10 Cost Contributors) with 1d/7d toggles; (2) coarse tracing: automatic sampled traces for p95+latency spikes and a lightweight link to the full tracing product (deferred); (3) simplified cost breakdown: show top 10 routes by total token spend and per-request median token cost, not full per-user or per-token drilling; (4) default sampling and prefix caching to limit ingest; (5) graceful degraded view when telemetry not available and clear guidance for Dedicated customers to enable extended modes. Defer: timeline zoom, per-request waterfall, full-span tracing, unlimited historical retention, and interactive cost allocation filters.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Three dashboard cards implemented and exposed in Console under 'Observability Lite' feature flag: Route Latency (P50/P95), Route Error Rate (5xx %), Top-10 Cost Contributors (daily rollup)
AC-2: Cards load within 600ms on average for typical queries; backend queries limited to 3s timeout and respect SLOs
AC-3: Tracing surface limited to sampled traces triggered by p95 latency anomalies; clicking a card opens a trace summary with a link to the full tracing workspace (deferred), no full-span UI in MVP
AC-4: Cost card reports top-10 routes with daily token spend and median tokens per-request; values are within 5% of billing data for top routes in initial 7-day window
AC-5: Feature is behind server-side flag and rollout can be toggled per-org; default off for Dedicated customers until capacity validated
AC-6: Telemetry fallbacks implemented: if metrics API returns 503 or timeout, UI surfaces a clear degraded message and retains last successful snapshot for up to 12 hours
AC-7: Automated e2e smoke tests validate card rendering, sample traces generation, and cost rollup correctness in the staging environment
AC-8: Operational dashboards for platform team created to monitor ingest rate, data errors, sampling rate, and additional costs; alerted if daily ingest > 1.5x forecast
decisions: Keep card count minimal (3) to reduce data model and UX complexity
Push full span tracing and deep cost exploration to post-MVP (tracked as PM-67110)
Default sampling rate set to 1% for traces with adaptive bumping on observed p95 anomaly
Avoid per-user cost breakdowns in MVP to limit data joins and PII implications
tradeoffs: Reduced visibility: engineers lose some ad-hoc debugging ability compared to full tracing but gain faster shipping and lower infra costs
Simplified cost estimates might hide edge-case spenders; we accept this to prevent scope creep
UX simplicity could require future migration work when extending cards to support filters and time ranges
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): behind flag for internal orgs only for 2 weeks, collect qualitative feedback and ingest metrics. Phase 2 (canary): enable for 5% of orgs in hosted, monitor platform ingest/latency and customer feedback. Phase 3 (gradual): increase to 50% with safety rollback; Dedicated orgs remain opt-in until capacity certification. Launch comms include migration notes and guidance for enabling deeper telemetry post-MVP.
